causalModel.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A firm crest above a shallow shelf: the stilt quarters step down from the crest to a tidal flat and a lighter quay. Big hulls anchor out on the 10 m plateau and their cargo comes ashore by lighter. The lightering is the city’s living.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; it will not appoint a ruler. The last party that had one killed the city.
causalModel.pressures: Hostile to the An-Xileel successor state and indispensable to a bay that must trade somewhere. It is also built over its own mass grave.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once. The rules forbid it.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: settlement-register.md §2 (M5, rebuilt smaller); lilmoth.md owner decision 2026-08-24 (smaller, lower, over a mass grave); 95-build-sequence.md (M5 quest band 35–60); Morrowind:Balmora as the ratio check at about 40 buildings.
scaleGrounding.why: Twenty-six households in bamboo huts and the tall block, at five to a household, give about 130 residents; the council, the patrol, the tenders, the licence and salvage staff and the lighter crews housed on the quay add 60 to 100 more. Fifty-three placed structures is a third more than Balmora’s forty, which is the right size for a major city rebuilt smaller than the one it replaced. Seventy named residents follows Morrowind’s ratio of named people to buildings.

candidates.why: The east face of the promontory. Section from the crest out: 21.9 m at 3640/6350, a 22.5° bluff, a 7.4 m bench at 3720/6350 (slope 2.5°), a tidal flat at 1.3–1.5 m from 3800 to 3860 (flood band 1–3, wet-season inundated), then 1.0 m of water at 3880, 3.8 m at 3920 and a 6.6 m roadstead plateau from 3960 to 4040. That is four buildable tiers and a drowned quarter in one 400 m run. The shallow shelf is 120 m wide, which is why large hulls anchor out and their cargo comes ashore by lighter (Lore:Lilmoth). 55 m from the approved anchor, well inside its 0.04 UV (296 m) tolerance.

candidates.rejectedBecause: The south-east embayment reaches 3.8 m of water 50 m off the shore and 15.5 m at 150 m. Deep water that close means a hull could berth alongside, which contradicts the record in Lore:Lilmoth that the city is built over shallow water and lighters its cargo. It also has no bench between the shore and the crest, so the city would be one tier, not three.
candidates.why: Shore at roughly 3790/6540, water 0.6 m at 3798/6548, 3.8 m at 3826/6576, 9.6 m at 3855/6605, 25.5 m at 3939/6689; the SE ray falls 18.6 m to the waterline over 280 m with no flat step.

candidates.rejectedBecause: The southern lagoon behind the spit is 0.4–0.6 m deep at 3600/6590–6630 and land again at 3600/6670. Nothing there can be drowned to dive depth, so the drowned quarter, the record's signature, would be a puddle. No lighter could reach open water.
candidates.why: Sheltered water and a natural breakwater, which is why it was measured at all: 2.0 m of land at 3600/6510, 1.05 m at 3600/6550, 0.4 m of water at 3600/6590, land at 1.6 m again at 3600/6670.

districts.notes: What the water left standing: the arch across the road, the north tower, two wall stubs and the rubble of the south tower. No new work is built into the masonry.

why.what: The north gate: the Imperial arch, its surviving tower and the broken curtain either side, on the road from Blackrose.
why.whyHere: The Imperial circuit met its road here and the rebuilders kept the gate because it stood.
why.whyNeighbours: The Argonian track begins where the road ends inside it; the Hist court is on the crest above.
why.playerPurpose: The land entrance to the city, the patrol post and the north-gate station.
why.microGeography: A 14–16 m shelf between the pond on the west and the crest on the east, the lowest dry crossing of the wall line.

districts.notes: The crest, 19–23 m: the third Hist inside a ring of poles open to the east, two lodges outside the ring, the vigil awning inside it.

why.what: The Hist court: the tree, its ring of poles, the two tenders’ lodges and the vigil awning.
why.whyHere: The third tree grew from the second’s root on the crest. The city bends round it.
why.whyNeighbours: The spine track passes its east opening; the gate is below it to the west and the council bench to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The Hist court scene, the minder and the second tender.
why.microGeography: The highest ground in the city, level for 20 m round the trunk and falling on every side.

districts.notes: The 11–13 m bench east of the crest: hall, record room, strongroom, market deck, elders’ house, council floor, factor’s house and the bell on the lip. The hall and the market deck stand square to the bench walk; every other piece is set a few degrees off it on its own piles, following the fall of the bench, because an Argonian quarter is not surveyed (97 C8, Part F).

why.what: The council crown: the hall, the record room and strongroom, the open council floor, the upper market deck and the tariff bell.
why.whyHere: The merchant council needs level ground above the flood with the quay in view; the bench is the widest such ground.
why.whyNeighbours: The spine track arrives from the court on its west; the bluff stair leaves from the bell on its east.
why.playerPurpose: The council quests, the tariff roll, the upper market and the bell that is seen from the bay.
why.microGeography: A level 12 m shelf 80 m long, falling 1 m to the north and 2 m to the south.

districts.notes: The tidal flat under the bluff, 1–3 m, wet-season flooded. A loop of walkway with a cross lane, fifteen huts and the tall block, every one on piles.

why.what: Pusbottom: the repopulated slum on the flat under the bluff, a loop of planks with huts on both sides.
why.whyHere: The cheapest ground in the city is the ground that floods; the poor and the criminal quarter took it back after 4E 48.
why.whyNeighbours: The bell and the council stand on the bluff above it; the quay is along its east side.
why.playerPurpose: The vault, the slaughter list, the agent, the broker and most of the city’s dwellings.
why.microGeography: A flat at 1–3 m between the bluff foot and the water, drained by the lanes’ pile lines.

districts.notes: The water’s edge: the deck, the lamp, the licence house, the lighter shed, the divers’ shed and the salvage bench, with the pier and the stair.

why.what: The lighter quay: the deck at the water’s edge with the sheds along the lane behind it and the pier into the channel.
why.whyHere: Cargo comes ashore by lighter and the lighters need a deck, a light, a licence and a shed.
why.whyNeighbours: Pusbottom is at its back; the drowned quarter lies off its face.
why.playerPurpose: The lighter-quay station, the licences, the divers and the boat services.
why.microGeography: A strip of flat at 0–2 m along the shore, its east piles in the shallows.

districts.notes: The low flat south of the bluff: seven fishers’ huts in two rows on the shore lane, a boat awning, a drying rack and the pole wall facing the estuary.

why.what: The shore quarter: the fishers’ row on the low flat south of Pusbottom, behind the Argonian pole wall.
why.whyHere: The fishers of the estuary live on the flat nearest their water and away from the cargo quay.
why.whyNeighbours: Pusbottom is north-east across the shore lane; the pole wall closes it on the east.
why.playerPurpose: The offering season, the recitation speakers and a canoe for the estuary.
why.microGeography: A 2 m flat that floods in the wet season, drained toward the estuary.

districts.notes: Old Imperial Lilmoth under 1–12 m of water: seven ruin pieces on the old street grid, the shrine outermost, the channel cut through the middle.

why.what: The drowned quarter: the sunken Imperial villas off the quay, from the ridge in the shallows to the shrine on the plateau edge.
why.whyHere: Imperial houses on this soil sank; the rebuilders left the quarter drowned and nobody builds on it.
why.whyNeighbours: The quay and the diving stair are inshore; the roadstead is at its outer edge.
why.playerPurpose: The dive scene, the salvage quests and the shrine.
why.microGeography: The shelf falls from 1 m off the quay to 12 m at the plateau, with the channel dredged through it.

districts.notes: A one-piece works district: the roofed dues board beside the quay lane. The board is a works-v1 prop and the kit-set rule (one set per district) gives it a district of its own, three metres by seven, inside the quay's ground.

why.what: The dues board: the roofed notice board on which the licence house posts the lightering dues and the lot prices.
why.whyHere: Lilmoth lives by lightering, and the dues are read by every crew before they go to the licence house window; the record's price list belongs in the open, not behind a door.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands across the quay lane from the licence house door and south of the quay lamp, on the line every lighter crew walks from the deck to the stair.
why.playerPurpose: The prices and dues of Cargo Off the Ledger are read here, and the board is where a forged notice can be pinned.
why.microGeography: Two driven posts on the dry flat at 2.3 m, a stride east of the lane planks and clear of the flood band.

parcels.orientationWhy: The arch is set square to the Blackwood-side road so the carriageway passes through its opening.
parcels.assetRef: mwkeep:tesak1243/mwimperialarchitecture/architecture/keep/exterior/walls/mwimparchwallgate01

why.what: The surviving Imperial gate arch, 7.3 m of ashlar standing across the road from Blackrose.
why.whyHere: The Imperial circuit needed a landward gate where its road met the rise. The rebuilders kept the arch because it was still standing.
why.whySpot: The arch sits on the 15 m saddle where the road leaves the wet ground west of the crest, the lowest dry crossing of the old wall line.
why.whyNeighbours: The guard tower adjoins its northern pier and the broken curtain runs on from both piers, so the gate reads as part of a wall rather than a lone arch.
why.playerPurpose: The threshold of the city on foot, where the council patrol stands and asks for a licence.
why.microGeography: The road climbs 2 m through the arch; the ground under the piers is a firm 14–15 m shelf between the pond on the west and the crest on the east.

parcels.orientationWhy: The tower shares the arch’s bearing, so its faces sit flush with the gate piers and the curtain beyond.
parcels.assetRef: mwkeep:tesak1243/mwimperialarchitecture/architecture/keep/exterior/mwimparchguardtower01

why.what: The squat Imperial gate tower, 6 m square and 13 m high, adjoining the north pier of the arch.
why.whyHere: The Imperial wall had a tower at each gate; this one did not fall in 4E 48 and the council patrol uses it as its post.
why.whySpot: It stands on the north side of the arch, on the same shelf, where a watcher on its top sees the whole length of the road back to the pond.
why.whyNeighbours: The arch on its south and the broken curtain on its north are the pieces it was built to join.
why.playerPurpose: The patrol post at the gate, the first interior inside the wall and the station for the north-gate quest scenes.
why.microGeography: Its footing falls 3 m across the base from the crest side to the road, so the tower is cut into the shelf, as the Imperial masonry here sank rather than stood on piles.

parcels.abutsWhy: The Morrowind Imperial keep set is authored so a guard tower butts the pier of its wall gate; the two pieces share a face.

parcels.orientationWhy: It continues the line of the tower northward, on the bearing of the old curtain.
parcels.assetRef: mwkeep:tesak1243/mwimperialarchitecture/architecture/keep/exterior/walls/mwimparchwall01destroyed01

why.what: A broken length of the Imperial curtain running north from the gate tower, its top fallen.
why.whyHere: The curtain ran from the gate up onto the crest; this is the piece that still stands next to the tower.
why.whySpot: It occupies the wall line immediately north of the tower, on the same shelf.
why.whyNeighbours: It joins the tower on one side and the standing west curtain on the other.
why.playerPurpose: A climbable stub that gives a view over the pond and back along the road.
why.microGeography: Its base steps up 0.5 m along the shelf toward the crest.

parcels.abutsWhy: A curtain segment is authored to butt the tower face in the Imperial keep set.

parcels.orientationWhy: It continues the line of the south pier of the arch, on the bearing of the old curtain.
parcels.assetRef: mwkeep:tesak1243/mwimperialarchitecture/architecture/keep/exterior/walls/mwimparchwall01destroyed02

why.what: A broken length of the Imperial curtain running south from the arch toward the pond.
why.whyHere: The curtain south of the gate ran down to the water; this is the piece that remains above ground.
why.whySpot: It sits on the wall line south of the arch, where the shelf begins to fall toward the pond.
why.whyNeighbours: It joins the arch on its north and ends at the rubble of the fallen south tower.
why.playerPurpose: It closes the gate yard on the south, so the road is the way into the city.
why.microGeography: The ground under it falls 0.6 m southward toward the pond.

parcels.abutsWhy: A curtain segment is authored to butt the gate pier in the Imperial keep set.

parcels.orientationWhy: The heap lies down the slope toward the pond, the direction in which the tower fell.
parcels.assetRef: mwkeep:tesak1243/mwimperialarchitecture/architecture/keep/rubbles/mwimparchrubblepile01

why.what: The rubble of the southern gate tower, an 11 m spread of ashlar left where it dropped.
why.whyHere: The gate had two towers; the southern one came down in the fighting of 4E 48 and the council has not cleared it.
why.whySpot: It lies at the south end of the wall line, on the falling ground between the curtain and the pond.
why.whyNeighbours: It marks the end of the wall stub and the edge of the pond.
why.playerPurpose: A find for a searcher: the tower stair is still open inside the heap.
why.microGeography: The heap has settled into ground that falls 3 m toward the pond, which is why the tower fell that way.

parcels.orientationWhy: The lodge is turned to face the Hist, so its opening looks across the court to the trunk.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut01

why.what: The tree-minder’s lodge, a bamboo hut on the west side of the court.
why.whyHere: The minder’s post rotates and whoever holds it must sleep within sight of the tree.
why.whySpot: It stands on the crest west of the court ring, 28 m from the trunk, outside the poles but facing the opening.
why.whyNeighbours: The second tender’s lodge sits on the opposite side of the court, so the two watchers are never in the same house.
why.playerPurpose: The minder’s home; the minder is the neutral broker of the city’s disputes.
why.microGeography: The crest here is 19–20 m and nearly level; the piles are short and the floor sits a step above the court.

parcels.orientationWhy: The lodge faces the Hist from the north, so the tender sees the trunk from the doorway.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

why.what: The second tender’s lodge, a bamboo hut on the north side of the court.
why.whyHere: City rule requires a second tender present whenever the minder listens to the tree.
why.whySpot: It stands on the northern edge of the crest, 36 m from the trunk, where the ground begins to fall toward the bench.
why.whyNeighbours: It is placed across the court from the minder’s lodge; the two doors face each other over the tree.
why.playerPurpose: The second witness in every Hist scene; the tender keeps the vigil roster.
why.microGeography: The crest falls 3 m across this hull toward the north, so the northern piles are longer than the southern.

parcels.orientationWhy: The open side of the awning faces the trunk, so the sitter watches the tree and not the court entrance.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/orcawninghalf01

why.what: An open hide awning on four poles inside the court, where the vigil is sat.
why.whyHere: The vigil is kept in the open, in sight of the tree and of anyone entering the court.
why.whySpot: It stands inside the eastern opening of the court ring, 16 m south-east of the trunk.
why.whyNeighbours: The court footpath from the spine passes its north side to the tree.
why.playerPurpose: The seat for the Hist court scene and the place where the minder receives visitors.
why.microGeography: The awning stands on the level top of the crest at 21 m.

parcels.orientationWhy: The long axis follows the council walkway, so the whole front is a step from the planks.
parcels.assetRef: bmv:architecture/stilthouse/stilthouseext

why.what: The council hall, the tallest stilt house in the city, 18 m long and three storeys under its ridge.
why.whyHere: The merchant council needs a covered floor for its sittings and a place for the tariff clerks.
why.whySpot: It stands on the 12 m bench north of the walkway, the widest level ground on the shoulder.
why.whyNeighbours: The record room is on its west, the strongroom behind it and the open council floor across the walkway.
why.playerPurpose: The council-hall station, the council-floor scene and the factor who gives the tariff quests.
why.microGeography: The bench falls 1 m to the north under the hull; the rear piles are longer.

parcels.orientationWhy: Set six degrees off the bench walk on its own piles, turned toward the 1 m fall to the north; its door still opens to the walk.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut01

why.what: The record room, a bamboo hut holding two centuries of customs books.
why.whyHere: The tariff is the council’s authority and its rolls have to be kept where the clerks sit.
why.whySpot: It is the first building on the bench west of the hall, where the spine arrives from the court.
why.whyNeighbours: The hall is its neighbour to the east; the strongroom is behind both.
why.playerPurpose: The tariff roll and the customs books that settle property claims.
why.microGeography: Level 12 m ground; the piles are short and even.

parcels.orientationWhy: Turned a few degrees off the bench line toward the strongroom path, so its door faces the path that serves it alone.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

why.what: The council strongroom, a bamboo hut behind the hall with the bonded goods inside.
why.whyHere: Goods held against unpaid duty need a locked room under the council’s eye.
why.whySpot: It stands behind the hall on the north edge of the bench, out of sight of the walkway.
why.whyNeighbours: The hall screens it from the market; the north curtain ruin lies beyond it.
why.playerPurpose: The strongroom loot and the pre-rebuild plan.
why.microGeography: The bench drops 1.5 m to the north here, so the rear piles stand in the fall.

parcels.orientationWhy: The deck lies along the walkway so stalls on it face the passing traffic.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/kothringi/stilthouseplatform

why.what: The upper walkway market: an open deck on piles with no walls. Its outline is a plain rectangle because it is a platform.
why.whyHere: The record says the upper market stands on the walkways above the quay, out of the flood.
why.whySpot: It is set south of the walkway where the bench begins to fall, so the deck stands level over the slope.
why.whyNeighbours: The hall faces it across the walkway; the elders’ house is the next building east.
why.playerPurpose: The upper-market station, the traders and the rumour pool of the city.
why.microGeography: The ground under the deck falls 2 m southward; the south piles are the longest on the bench.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door is on the walkway side, opposite the hall.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

why.what: The elders’ house, where the retired Shadowscales who settle disputes are found.
why.whyHere: In Lilmoth people look to their elders, including retired Shadowscales, for judgement.
why.whySpot: It stands on the walkway between the market deck and the council floor, in the middle of civic ground.
why.whyNeighbours: The market deck is west of it and the council floor east.
why.playerPurpose: The Retired Rota quest and a source of judgement outside the council.
why.microGeography: The bench is level here at 12 m.

parcels.orientationWhy: The stone ring is set to the fall of the bench edge on which it is dug in, a few degrees off the walk, because a ring of stones follows its ground and not a survey.
parcels.assetRef: histtree:skyfall/sleeping tree overhaul/rune circle

why.what: The council floor, a ring of standing stones open to the sky.
why.whyHere: The council sits in the open when it rules on a tariff, so the ruling is seen.
why.whySpot: It stands at the east end of the bench beside the bell, where the quay is in view below.
why.whyNeighbours: The bell kiosk is next to it; the elders’ house is on its west.
why.playerPurpose: The council-floor scene and the council-standing mark.
why.microGeography: The stones are set into the fall at the south edge of the bench, which drops 2 m across the ring.

parcels.orientationWhy: Set six degrees off the bench walk on its own piles, turned toward the 2 m fall to the south; its door still opens to the walk.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut01

why.what: The council factor’s house, a bamboo hut east of the hall.
why.whyHere: The factor who holds the tariff line lives on the bench, within a few steps of the hall.
why.whySpot: It fills the gap between the hall and the bell, on the north side of the walkway.
why.whyNeighbours: The hall is on its west and the bell kiosk on its east.
why.playerPurpose: The quest-giver of the tariff line, at home in the evening.
why.microGeography: The bench falls 1 m northward under it.

parcels.orientationWhy: The kiosk is set on the walkway’s bearing so the bell hangs over the lip of the bench toward the quay.
parcels.assetRef: bmv:architecture/citebosmer/passerelles/kiosque/kiosk01

why.what: The tariff bell: a 21 m timber kiosk tower on the lip of the bench, with the bell and a lamp at its top.
why.whyHere: The bell is rung when the tariff changes and when a hull lies at the roadstead; it has to be heard on the quay.
why.whySpot: It stands at the east end of the bench, 9 m above the flat, where the tower top is 30 m over the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The council floor and the factor’s house are beside it; the bluff stair leaves from its foot.
why.playerPurpose: The first thing seen from the bay and the mark that leads from the quay up to the council.
why.microGeography: The piles stand on the break of slope on 9–10 m ground; the lamp platform rides above it.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its long axis lies along the bluff foot, 8° off the west lane, so the building fits the strip between the slope and the lane.
parcels.assetRef: bmv:architecture/stilthouse/stilthouseext

why.what: The tall block of Pusbottom, a three-storey stilt house against the bluff foot, let by the room.
why.whyHere: Pusbottom was repopulated by people who could pay for a room and not for a house.
why.whySpot: It stands at the north-west corner of the district, where the bluff shelters it and the stair from the bench comes down.
why.whyNeighbours: The west lane of the loop passes its east side; the stair foot is at its north end.
why.playerPurpose: The rooming house of the slum: hired rooms, the vault entrance quest and the broker’s office.
why.microGeography: The flat here is 2–3 m and the bluff rises behind it; the piles are level with the walkway.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 8° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned east onto the planks, with its back to the bluff.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut01

why.what: A bamboo hut whose floor hides the shaft down to the flooded municipal vault.
why.whyHere: The old vault lies under this part of the flat. Whoever holds the hut holds the way down.
why.whySpot: It is the first hut on the west side of the loop, hard against the bluff foot where the vault roof is shallowest.
why.whyNeighbours: The tall block is to its north; the slaughter-list house is across the lane.
why.playerPurpose: The way into the Vault Beneath Pusbottom.
why.microGeography: The ground is 2 m and firm; the shaft goes down through the old fill.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 6° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned west onto the planks, toward the bluff-side huts.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

why.what: A bamboo hut in which a list of the names from the Slaughter is kept.
why.whyHere: Somebody in Pusbottom wrote down who died in 4E 48. The list stayed in the family.
why.whySpot: It stands on the east side of the west lane, opposite the vault house.
why.whyNeighbours: The vault house faces it; the agent’s room is two doors south.
why.playerPurpose: The slaughter-list evidence for the main quest.
why.microGeography: Level 2 m ground; the piles are a hand above the wet-season mark.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 4° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned east onto the planks, with its back to the bluff.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

why.what: The house of the broker who sells deeds to emptied Rockpark houses.
why.whyHere: Deeds to plague houses sell in a slum, where buyers ask few questions.
why.whySpot: It is the second hut on the west side of the loop, under the bluff.
why.whyNeighbours: The vault house is north of it and the reed-cutter’s house south.
why.playerPurpose: The Untouched House quest begins here.
why.microGeography: The bluff foot keeps the ground here dry at 2 m.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 7° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned west onto the planks, toward the bluff-side huts.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut01

why.what: A rented room in a bamboo hut, kept by the deniable An-Xileel agent.
why.whyHere: An agent of the successor state cannot live openly in a city that hates it; a room in Pusbottom is the cover.
why.whySpot: It is on the east side of the west lane, one door south of the slaughter-list house.
why.whyNeighbours: The broker’s house faces it across the lane.
why.playerPurpose: The agent quest-giver and the Pusbottom Remembers confrontation.
why.microGeography: Level ground at 2 m, like its neighbours.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 17° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned east onto the planks, with its back to the bluff.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut01

why.what: A reed-cutter’s hut, with the cut reeds stacked under the floor.
why.whyHere: The reed fringe south of the quay is cut by Pusbottom households for thatch and matting.
why.whySpot: It is the third hut on the west side, where the bluff begins to draw back from the lane.
why.whyNeighbours: The broker’s house is north of it and the poler’s hut south.
why.playerPurpose: A dwelling to enter; the cutter knows the reed fringe and what lies in it.
why.microGeography: The flat is 2 m here and floods a hand deep at the wet-season peak.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 19° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned west onto the planks, toward the bluff-side huts.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

why.what: The house of the family who recognised their own goods in a licensed salvage lot.
why.whyHere: Salvage from the drowned quarter comes up under licence; the drowned owners’ heirs live in Pusbottom.
why.whySpot: It is the third hut on the east side of the west lane.
why.whyNeighbours: The agent’s room is north of it and the dice-runner’s hut south.
why.playerPurpose: The Licensed Lot quest.
why.microGeography: Level ground at 2 m, a hand above the wet-season mark.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut stands 20° off the west lane, as its household set its own piles; the opening is turned east onto the planks, with its back to the bluff.
parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/bamboohut02

routes.why: The last stretch of the Imperial road from Blackrose, surveyed straight to the gate arch, which stands across it.
The Imperial road inside the arch, running straight to the lantern at the foot of the crest, where Imperial Lilmoth ended and the Argonian track begins.
The worn track from the gate yard over the southern shoulder of the crest, passing the Hist court on its left hand, down to the council bench.
The tenders’ path from the spine round the south of the court ring to the minder’s door.
The short path from the spine through the opening in the court ring to the trunk.
The path from the spine north-west to the second tender’s lodge on the crest edge.
The path from the council walkway round the east end of the hall to the strongroom door.
The timber stair down the bluff from the bell to the Pusbottom junction, 9 m of fall in 35 m.

canals.why: The dredged navigation line from the pier head to the roadstead, the one water deep enough for a laden lighter across the shelf.

boardwalks.why: The council walkway, the one surveyed line in the Argonian city, laid straight along the bench from the spine track to the bell.
The spine across the north of Pusbottom from the stair foot to the quay deck, the busiest planks in the city.
The loop walkway of Pusbottom, west lane, south lane and east lane, with the huts on both sides and the quay deck at its end.
The cross lane through the middle of the loop, from the spine to the south lane, serving the porters’ row.
The quay lane along the water’s edge from the lantern at the stair foot past the licence house and the lamp to the deck.
The boardwalk from the south-west corner of Pusbottom over the wet flat to the fishers’ row and the boat awning.
The lighter pier from the quay deck east to the head of the channel, where the lighters come alongside.
The short pier from the divers’ shed to the diving stair.

fences.why: The standing Imperial curtain from the gate tower north up the west face of the crest, 13 m high, what the water and the An-Xileel left.
The broken north curtain along the shoulder above the council bench, fallen to half its height.
The ring of driven poles round the Hist court, closed on the north, west and south and open to the spine on the east: walled and open, as the city rule requires.
fences.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/kothringi/tamu_woodpole01

fences.why: The Argonian wall facing the estuary: a line of driven poles along the shore of the fishers’ quarter, the city’s wall on the side the Imperials never built.

why.whyHere: Big hulls anchor out on the 10 m plateau because the shelf is too shallow; the mark shows them where.
why.whySpot: It stands at the east end of the dredged channel on the edge of the plateau.
why.whyNeighbours: The channel runs from it to the pier head; the shrine lies south-west.
why.playerPurpose: The point at which a passenger from a ship transfers to a lighter; the end of the channel.
why.microGeography: Driven into the 10 m plateau where the shelf ends.

landmarks.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/ruins/xanmeer/totem02

why.what: The idol of Xhon-Mehl the Fisher, a 2 m carved totem at the back of the shrine.
why.whyHere: The shrine to the Ancestral Organ Lord of Lilmoth was in the lower town and drowned with it.
why.whySpot: It stands against the east wall of the shrine block, facing the opening.
why.whyNeighbours: The altar block is in front of it and the marker at the opening.
why.playerPurpose: The focus of the Offerings in the Mouth quest.
why.microGeography: On the bed at 12 m, inside the block.

landmarks.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/ruins/xanmeer/totem03

why.what: The altar block of the shrine, where the fishers’ offerings are laid.
why.whyHere: Offerings to the Fisher are still made each season by the shore households.
why.whySpot: It stands in the middle of the shrine block in front of the idol.
why.whyNeighbours: The idol is behind it and the marker at the opening.
why.playerPurpose: Where the offering is placed in the quest.
why.microGeography: On the bed at 12 m, in the middle of the block.

landmarks.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/ruins/xanmeer/runicstone

why.what: An inscribed stone at the shrine opening, its face turned out to the channel.
why.whyHere: The marker names the god to a diver arriving from the stair.
why.whySpot: It stands at the western opening of the shrine block.
why.whyNeighbours: The altar and idol are behind it inside the block.
why.playerPurpose: The mark by which the shrine is found in the dark water.
why.microGeography: On the bed at 12 m, at the west opening of the block.

why.what: The lighter berth at the pier head, where laden lighters come alongside.
why.whyHere: The shelf is too shallow for a hull, so cargo comes ashore in lighters and needs a berth at the channel head.
why.whyNeighbours: The pier runs from the quay deck to it and the channel runs from it to the roadstead.
why.playerPurpose: The arrival point by boat and the departure point for the lighter flotilla and the Meerhleel boat.
why.microGeography: The piles stand at the head of the dredged channel in 4 m of water.

why.what: The diving stair: a timber stair off the divers’ pier into the channel.
why.whyHere: The salvage divers enter the water from a stair, not from the deck, so the deck stays clear for cargo.
why.whyNeighbours: The divers’ shed is at its head and the drowned villa floors lie below it.
why.playerPurpose: The diving-stair station and the start of every dive into the drowned quarter.
why.microGeography: The stair drops from the flat at 0 m to the bed at 2 m.

why.what: The tender mooring at the roadstead, where the big hulls lie and the lighters load.
why.whyHere: The 10 m plateau is the nearest water to the city in which a hull can lie.
why.whyNeighbours: The roadstead mark stands over it and the channel runs from it to the pier.
why.playerPurpose: Where a ship passenger is put into a lighter; the sea-side end of the city.
why.microGeography: Piles driven into the plateau edge in 10 m of water.

combatSpaces.why: The council patrol holds the gate yard when the hostility flip to hunted closes the city; the yard between the arch and the lantern is the open ground for that fight.
Cargo Off the Ledger and A Body in the Lot both end on the deck. The guarded flip puts the patrol here first.
Pusbottom Remembers and the vault heist can turn to a fight in the lanes; the two-metre planks between huts are the tight class.
The Second Room and Short of Divers put a predator in the drowned hall; the fight is underwater between the floor slab and the block.

approaches.sequence: From the road on the flat west of the pond the crown of the Hist shows over the trees on the crest, 40 m above the traveller. The road bends round the pond and the gate tower and the standing curtain hide the tree; the arch and the tower are what is seen. Through the arch the track climbs the shoulder and the tree comes back on the left hand behind its ring of poles; at the top of the shoulder the bell kiosk shows ahead and the bay opens beyond it.
approaches.wayfinding: Keep the pond on the left, go through the arch to the lantern and follow the track uphill with the pole ring on the left until the bell shows ahead.
approaches.notes: The road arrives from the west-north-west; the city calls it the north gate because the road is the road north to Blackrose. The last 200 m bend twice, round the pond and over the shoulder.

approaches.fromDirection: east, from the roadstead in Oliis Bay
approaches.sequence: From a lighter at the roadstead the bell kiosk on the lip of the bench reads first, 30 m above the water, with the quay lamp below it and the Hist crown behind and higher. Along the channel the ridge block breaks the water on the right hand and hides the lamp for a moment; then the pier head, the quay deck and the sheds along the lane come into view under the bluff.
approaches.wayfinding: Steer for the upper lamp, keep the ridge block to starboard and come alongside at the pier head; the deck is the end of the pier and the stair up to the bell leaves from the lane behind it.
approaches.notes: The lighter takes the dredged line; a swimmer from the roadstead crosses the drowned quarter and reaches the diving stair first.

approaches.fromDirection: south, along the estuary shore from the high junction and the hist-less fringe
approaches.sequence: From the flat to the south the bell kiosk stands over the bluff and the Hist crown behind it. The pole wall and the fishers’ roofs hide the bluff foot as the walker comes up the shore; the shore lane appears between the pole wall and the mangrove; at the corner of Pusbottom the tall block and the lanes are seen close under the bell.
approaches.wayfinding: Walk the shore with the water on the right until the pole wall; the lane between the last fisher’s hut and the wall leads to the corner of the loop; the stair to the bell is at the far end of the west lane.
approaches.notes: The high junction tower at 3773, 6496 stands 15 m outside the pole wall and is the mid-way mark on this approach.

assetConstraints: settlement-mud-v1 is forbidden here: Lilmoth is Murkmire reed/stilt culture and material-culture.md forbids blending the two Argonian building cultures in one settlement.

composite:quay/stone-quay-with-stilt-house is forbidden here: it welds an Imperial keep stone dock to an Argonian stilt house, which is both the owner’s 2026-09-04 worked example of a composition nobody authored and a two-culture blend inside one mesh.

Dock systems are never butted mid-run: the BM&V Dagon Fel jetty system builds the lighter pier, HTBM’s tamu_ lashed-plank boardwalk builds the shore boardwalks; the change of system happens at the quay deck.
No new work is built into the Imperial masonry in district.lilmoth.north-gate.
